subject: Mid-run signal check: scope-trim proposals & dep commitments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-run signal check: scope-trim proposals & dep commitments

Team —

Quick mid-run pulse before QBR prep. We ran the mid-quarter measurements last week; highlights attached (latency_heatmap_aug.png) and a dependency tracker with the current asks (dep_tracker_q3_v2.xlsx). TL;DR: we’re behind on the "adaptive prefix caching" work that’s driving 30% token-cost saving in the hosted tier. If we don’t reduce scope, we risk slipping the rollout past the QBR window and miss expected cost reduction targets.

Options I’m proposing (short):

1) Option A — Minimal ship: shipping prefix cache but removing per-tenant hot-key routing. Saves ~18% cost, lower infra complexity, fits with current staffing.
2) Option B — Full ship: include tenant routing and autoscaler tuning. Saves ~30% cost but requires 3 extra sprints from infra and platform (we don’t have confirmed commits).
3) Option C — Stop & swap: postpone caching work, prioritize smaller optimizations (token batching improvements + compiler kernel tweak) that net ~10% and are less dependent on infra.

Asks: please reply with: (a) which option you support, (b) names of engineers you can commit (if Option B), and (c) any blockers we must escalate now (procurements, infra quotas, security reviews). I’ll consolidate decisions and update the QBR one-pager.

Attachments: dep_tracker_q3_v2.xlsx, latency_heatmap_aug.png, draft QBR one-pager stub attached.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-run signal check: scope-trim proposals & dep commitments

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear framing. I recommend Option A as the default given the QBR timeline. The full ship (Option B) is attractive economically, but we don’t have the infra FTEs guaranteed this quarter without shifting commits from other high-criticality work (notably dedicated capacity autoscaler).

I can commit the infra lead (Rohit Sharma) for 2 sprints on the caching platform-level work if Aditya can confirm 1 backend engineer and 1 SRE for tenant routing. If we can't get those commits by EOD Friday, we switch to Option A and focus on the compiler/kernel follow-ups you noted.

Blockers:
- We need an 8-week SOC2 audit exception for the tenant routing proof-of-concept (security has flagged data isolation tests). Naomi, can security expedite a runbook?
- Cloud quota increase for prefetch cache nodes (I submitted request; awaiting cloud PO).

I'll hold Rohit in a soft-commit til Friday.

—Vivek
VP, Engineering
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-run signal check: scope-trim proposals & dep commitments

Vivek / team —

I support Option B if we can make the following guarantees:
- Platform will provide 1 backend engineer (I propose Tanner Lee) + 1 SRE (Priya Natarajan) for the routing work for 3 sprints.
- Product will freeze any new feature requests touching inference runtime until the cache rollout completes.

Questions:
1) Is the SOC2 exception strictly gating the PoC? If so, Naomi, what's the expected timeline to close that runbook?
2) Can we reduce the infra quota risk by staging tenant routing behind a flag for 10 pilot tenants (reduce node footprint)?

If those are affirmative, Option B is high-value and worth pulling rosters. If not, I'll align to Option A and we’ll pursue the compiler/batching wins.

--Aditya
Director, Platform
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-run signal check: scope-trim proposals & dep commitments

All —

I can prioritize the SOC2 runbook for the tenant routing PoC. Target: initial risk assessment + test plan by Thursday COB (2026-09-03). If the PoC only targets 10 pilot tenants, that lowers the risk surface and should be approvable faster.

A few asks for QBR visibility: please add two slides to the one-pager that show (a) direct dollar impact to hosted customers (example customers affected) and (b) fallback plan if the tenant routing PoC hits audit constraints. Sales/CS wants a clear customer message. Marissa — can you add Acme Analytics to the appendix (they're on the pilot list and Olga is copied here)?

Naomi
Head of Security & Compliance
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrova <olga@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: decision and next steps (Option B soft-commit -> staged pilot)

Team — thanks for the rapid replies. Summary / decision: we’ll go with a staged Option B (soft-commit) under the following constraints:

Decisions / commitments:
- Staged pilot of tenant routing behind a flag for up to 10 pilot tenants. This reduces infra footprint and should speed approvals.
- Rohit Sharma (Infra) — soft-commit from Vivek for 2 sprints starting 2026-09-06.
- Tanner Lee (Backend) & Priya Natarajan (SRE) — Aditya confirmed availability; formal calendar invites inbound.
- Naomi: proceed with SOC2 runbook prioritization for pilot -> test plan by COB 2026-09-03.
- Marissa/Product: I will update the QBR one-pager with the two requested slides and add Acme Analytics in the appendix. Draft link: https://docs.redwood.ai/drive/QBR/2026/q3-midrun-brief

Blockers / open items:
- Cloud PO for quota increase: Vivek to follow up with procurement and loop in finance if needed.
- If SOC2 runbook is delayed beyond Friday, we fallback immediately to Option A and re-scope for QBR.

Next steps (this week):
- Aditya: send calendar invites for Tanner/Priya and confirm sprint allocations.
- Vivek: confirm Rohit’s schedule and raise the cloud quota ticket reference number.
- Naomi: share runbook draft and list of tests we’ll need for the pilot.
- Marissa: update dep_tracker_q3_v2.xlsx and QBR one-pager; share final slides by EOD Friday.

Attachments: updated dep_tracker_q3_v2.xlsx (sheet: staged-pilot), qbr_one_pager_draft.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
